Example reports

Source: vignettes/articles/example_report.Rmd
example_report.Rmd

Two reports from render_report(), both run against the full Fake NHS Trust synthetic dataset read through its fakehospdata package, leaving out its answers schema (the mess log and truth tables are the dataset’s answer key, not part of the trust’s warehouse). Each report is a single self-contained HTML page with three tabs, one per phase, and every table in it can be filtered and downloaded. They are regenerated by the example-reports workflow on the repository’s Actions tab, run by hand.

Report Dataset Sampling threshold Tables Tables sampled Columns Rows in total Phases 2 and 3 Run time Rendered
sampled full set 1,000,000 rows 45 7 518 54,368,976 Phase 1 only: this was a sampled check, where not every row of the largest tables was reviewed. The full check below shows phases 2 and 3. 14 s 2026-10-25 13:03 UTC
full full set none 45 0 518 54,368,976 Shown: 90 foreign key candidates and the table clusters 17 s 2026-10-25 13:03 UTC

Sampled report

The default way to run the package on a large warehouse. Every table is inventoried and every column profiled, but tables above the sampling threshold are profiled on a sample of their rows, so the run is quick and the largest tables cost no more than the smallest. Phase 1 is complete; the phase 2 and 3 tabs explain that a full check is needed for clustering and keys.

Open the sampled report (opens in a new tab, 2.3 MB, rendered 2026-10-25 13:03 UTC)

Full report

Every row of every table is profiled, so distinct counts and uniqueness are exact and phases 2 and 3 are produced: the table clusters with a proposed canonical member for each group, the primary key candidates, and the foreign key candidates with their evidence and confidence. On a large SQL Server warehouse this is the slower run; on DuckDB and Parquet it is usually the quicker one.

Open the full report (opens in a new tab, 2.4 MB, rendered 2026-10-25 13:03 UTC)

To make one for your own database:

library(DBinventory)
inventory_run("Driver={ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server};Server=...;Database=...;Trusted_Connection=yes;",
              organisation = "Your NHS Trust", store = "dw_inventory.sqlite", report = "dw_inventory.html")
